properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The 16 remaining sites are keccak code-hash/tx-hash identity comparisons for matching — account-has-code checks against KECCAK_EMPTY, receipt↔transaction matching, bytecode-hash equality in verify/script/zksync — in a local dev toolchain. They are digest comparisons, not secret-dependent MAC verification; no adversarial timing oracle exists in a CLI/local-node context. Uninteresting but real; kept for completeness.

properties.value: k256 0.11.6 supplies secp256k1 ECDSA — the Ethereum transaction-signing algorithm, exercised through the local signer path (alloy-signer-local, crates/wallets) and the EVM. The algorithm is fixed by the Ethereum protocol: secp256k1 ECDSA is consensus-critical, so this is observable here but replaceable only by an ecosystem-wide protocol change (a future PQ signature EIP / account abstraction), not by this repo. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto ecdsa crate 0.16 (crates/cheatcodes/Cargo.toml:62) — the prehash-ECDSA signing framework behind k256/p256 signing in the vm.sign and vm.signP256 cheatcodes (crypto.rs:16 imports SigningKey/hazmat); crates/wallets/src/error.rs:54 wraps ecdsa::Error for the signer stack. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: NIST P-256 ECDSA via the p256 crate: vm.signP256 (sign_prehashed, crypto.rs:402-411) and vm.publicKeyP256 cheatcodes, with key validation at crypto.rs:431 (validate_private_key::<p256::NistP256>); the two cheatcodes.json sites are the generated metadata for those cheatcodes. Deliberately distinct from the EVM's secp256k1 — this is the FIPS curve exposed for non-EVM signature testing; migrates to ML-DSA when PQ signatures are needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 capability shipped via ring 0.17.14 — the rustls crypto provider force-installed by install_crypto_provider() (crates/cli/src/utils/mod.rs). No first-party Ed25519 signing/verifying call site was found; the algorithm is available in the shipped TLS stack (ring's Ed25519 is used for certificate signature verification of Ed25519 certs during TLS handshakes). Migration would be ML-DSA-65, and practically means moving rustls to the aws-lc-rs provider.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: p256 crate 0.13.2 lockfile entry — the same dependency LIB-2a9c88d0 records under the library name; this is the algorithm view (ECDSA on NIST P-256) of the crate powering vm.signP256 (crates/cheatcodes/src/crypto.rs:431).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 arrives via ring 0.17.14 — the crypto provider Foundry pins process-wide for rustls (crates/cli/src/utils/mod.rs:242 installs rustls::crypto::ring as default), behind reqwest's rustls-tls for every outbound HTTPS connection (RPC endpoints, Etherscan, Flashbots). TLS key exchange is classical X25519/ECDHE only; ring 0.17 offers no ML-KEM groups, so all RPC/API traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-later exposed. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 ships as the alternative KDF of Ethereum keystore v3 (kdf: "pbkdf2"): the pbkdf2 crate is locked as an eth-keystore dependency, and keystores created by other tools using pbkdf2 decrypt through the same wrapper chain as the scrypt ones (crates/cast/src/cmd/wallet/mod.rs, crates/wallets/src/signer.rs — see the keystore finding filed this hunt). First-party code never selects the KDF directly; eth-keystore honors the file's kdfparams (EIP-2335 recommends c≥262144). LIB-ea49d4c1 is the same

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 crate locked in Cargo.lock — transitively shipped (revm's SHA-256 precompile, alloy, etc.); the binaries execute SHA-256 inside the EVM precompile. The only first-party reference found is a trace decoder (crates/evm/traces/src/decoder/precompiles.rs:170 struct Sha256) that labels precompile calls in decoded traces — it performs no hashing itself. SHA-256 is PQ-comfortable (Grover gives only a square-root speedup); CNSA 2.0 prefers SHA-384. LIB-ea6b9ac4 is the same sighting under a crate ide

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: aes-gcm crate locked in Cargo.lock with no first-party call site found — it ships transitively (e.g. secret-vault-value/gcloud-sdk for GCP KMS, alloy/zksync paths). Presence is the inventory question: the binary carries an AES-GCM implementation. AES-128-GCM retains a 64-bit quantum margin under Grover; CNSA 2.0 prefers AES-256-GCM, and no first-party code pins the key size here.

properties.value: jsonwebtoken is locked via two paths: alloy-rpc-types-engine (engine-API JWT auth) and gcloud-sdk (Google OAuth tokens for the GCP KMS signer). The live first-party use is build_auth() in crates/common/src/provider/runtime_transport.rs:340-344 (filed as a finding): cast/forge take --jwt-secret (env ETH_RPC_JWT_SECRET, crates/cli/src/opts/rpc.rs:59), the secret is hex-decoded into alloy's JwtSecret and an HS256 token is signed per request. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 support arrives with rustls 0.23 (locked in Cargo.lock): the binaries' RPC HTTPS/WSS sessions negotiate TLS 1.3 by default. The PQ caveat is the provider, not the version — with ring installed (install_crypto_provider, crates/cli/src/utils/mod.rs:242) the 1.3 handshake still runs classical-only key exchange; X25519MLKEM768 hybrid groups require the aws-lc-rs provider. Version floor is fine; provider choice is the gap.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto hmac 0.12.1, consumed transitively at two live sites: engine-API JWT auth signs HS256 with the user's --jwt-secret via alloy-rpc-types-engine → jsonwebtoken (crates/common/src/provider/runtime_transport.rs:342-344), and eth-keystore's MAC verifies keystore-file integrity on the decrypt path (crates/wallets/src/signer.rs:348). HMAC-SHA256 is Grover-weakened (128-bit) but not Shor-broken; the keystore MAC algorithm is fixed by the Ethereum V3 keystore format.
